page_title: Vanna 2.0 – Build Agents Your Users Can Actually Use

summary.name: Vanna
summary.one_liner: Vanna is an open source framework for building SQL agents that let users query company databases in natural language, with optional hosted admin features.
use_cases: Letting non-SQL users ask questions of company databases in plain English
Generating insights without writing SQL by hand
Adding access-controlled data querying to production agents
Multi-turn conversational analytics over systems of record
summary.what_it_does: Vanna is an open source framework for building agents that answer natural-language questions by querying databases. It states that it works with any LLM provider and any database, and supports multi-database and multi-turn conversations. The framework includes access control so that users see only what they are permitted to see. Optional hosted admin features are listed, including access control, observability with metrics and tracing, hosted agent memory via a vector database, secure file storage, audit logs, and long-term data retention. The page also mentions copy-paste configuration code for getting started.
notable: Open source framework that works with any LLM provider and database
Optional hosted admin features: access control, observability, agent memory, audit logs
Rich UI components and quota management for production agents
caveats: Hosted admin features are optional and appear to be a separate offering from the open source framework; their pricing is not stated on the page
Pricing tiers and exact hosted costs are not given on the page
